author: blu
body: It is a record layer only. The handshake that establishes the keys is not here; a DtlsKeys is what a completed handshake hands over, and this chapter takes it as given. That split is deliberate: the record layer is agnostic to how the peer was authenticated, so it can be built and proven before that question is settled.

author: blu
body: Section: Sequence Number Encryption is the part most easily got wrong, and getting it wrong produces a record that verifies perfectly against itself and against nothing else. Two orderings matter, both quoted from the RFC below: the AEAD runs FIRST, over the header carrying the PLAINTEXT sequence number, and only then is the sequence number on the wire masked -- with a mask drawn from the AEAD's own ciphertext.
